evals.prompt: We run DevFest Lyonnais, about 600 people, once a year in March. Four volunteer organizers, all with day jobs. Our talk recordings already go up on our own Vimeo page within a month of each edition and the transcripts land on our blog. The team voted 3 to 1 to launch a fortnightly podcast starting in April, and two of us want the fortnightly rhythm on the website as soon as we agree on it. Nobody has said who would run it between March and next March. Write us the plan.
evals.expected_output: A posture recommendation that declines the fortnightly show: no channel (or archive-only) recommended outright, both original-content rungs deleted rather than demoted because nobody owns the quiet months, the unagreed public rhythm refused, and the decline written down as a decision with a reopening condition.
expectations: Does not deliver a fortnightly episode plan or publishing calendar as the answer
Recommends the no-channel posture, or archive-only, rather than an original-content channel
States that no channel is a real answer and a legitimate outcome, not a failure to plan
Deletes both original-content rungs from the menu rather than ranking or demoting them, on the grounds that nobody is named for the quiet months
Identifies the absence of a named owner for the months between editions as the blocking fact
Treats the existing Vimeo page and blog as evidence that the derivatives already have somewhere to publish
Refuses to publish a fortnightly cadence that no named person has agreed to hold
Names announcing a cadence nobody agreed to as a deleted option rather than a cheaper version of running a channel
Invents no episode interval, publishing frequency or subscriber figure of its own
States that the decline should be written down, with the condition that would reopen the question
Asks whether a portfolio decision to have a recurring media property was ever made, or routes that question to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-portfolio-strategy
Specifies no microphones, recorders, editing software or signal-path detail
Makes no claim that the show would sell tickets or fill seats

evals.prompt: I host the show for Kubernetes Nord, one conference a year, around 900 people. We have four episodes recorded: three interviews with people who spoke at our last edition, and one roundtable with two of those speakers plus my co-organizer Priya and a surprise drop-in from a sponsor's staff engineer. All four speakers signed our standard recording consent when they confirmed their talks last year, which covers AV capture and publication of the talk video. Our lawyer is expensive and I would rather not go back to her. Can we publish all four this month, and what do I need on file?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to treat the stage consent as covering the episodes, a requirement for an episode-specific release from every participant including hosts and the drop-in, the wording routed to counsel, and a named custodian with a retention decision.
expectations: States that the signed stage consent does not cover these episodes
Requires a separate, episode-specific release for each episode
Requires a release from every participant, not only the invited guests
Explicitly includes the host and the co-organizer Priya among those who must sign
Explicitly includes the sponsor's staff engineer who dropped into the roundtable
States that releases are collected before recording, so the four already-recorded episodes cannot publish until the releases exist
Refuses to publish any recording the consent record does not cover
Distinguishes the two instruments by what each covers: a talk delivered to a room in a stated format with a stated opt-out, versus a conversation recorded for publication on a standing property
Routes the release's actual wording to the organizer's own counsel rather than drafting enforceable terms
Names no jurisdiction and quotes no retention period
Names a single custodian who holds the episode release records
Does not re-open the event's speaker relationship or amend the existing stage-consent instrument to cover the episodes

evals.prompt: Our show for Berlin Infra Days is about 40 episodes in and we have burned through the 34 past speakers we had permission to contact. Two things on the table. Our platinum sponsor Vaultwright has offered us a guest every quarter, their VP of Engineering, no money changes hands, they just want the slot. And we are thinking of opening a public pitch-us form. Right now nobody on the team reviews anything, I book whoever replies first. What should the pipeline look like?
evals.expected_output: A sourcing pipeline that deletes the sponsor-supplied slot and the unreviewed open pitch rather than ranking them, names a vetting owner with a checkable bar, and states the promotion conditions for the remaining rungs.
expectations: Deletes the sponsor-supplied guest slot from the sourcing menu rather than ranking it low or listing it as a cheap option
States that a guest slot given because a sponsor asked for it converts the property into sponsor inventory
Routes any sponsored episode to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-sponsor-value-proposition as a sponsorship decision made there
States that a sponsored episode must be disclosed as one if it happens
Does not treat 'no money changes hands' as making the sponsor slot an editorial booking
Deletes the open pitch from the menu while no vetting owner exists, rather than ranking it
Requires a named vetting owner with a written bar before any public call opens
States that a published call needs a stated bar, a named reviewer and a stated answer window
States that booking whoever replies first is not a pipeline: availability is not fit and enthusiasm is not a bar
Produces a vetting bar made of checkable questions rather than desirable attributes such as engaging or well-known
Routes the conduct half of the bar to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-code-of-conduct instead of restating a policy
States the promotion conditions for cold outbound rather than recommending it unconditionally

Reuses the qualification and outreach craft from samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-speaker-sourcing and samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-speaker-cold-outreach instead of rebuilding it for the show

evals.prompt: Sponsorship lead for ShipIt Conf here. I need one page for the board on what our YouTube channel does for the conference. We have 12,000 subscribers, views are up 40% year over year, and I want a line in there saying the channel is our top-of-funnel for ticket sales, since we link the ticket page in every description. Our marketing agency's deck for a similar conference showed millions of added views and 30,000 new subscribers as proof their channel drove ticket sales. Write the page.
evals.expected_output: A two-direction feed map with every path marked EXISTS or ASPIRATIONAL, the ticket-page path marked ASPIRATIONAL, the seats-filled claim refused, and the agency evidence identified as channel-growth numbers with no registration figure attached.
expectations: Refuses to state that the channel is top-of-funnel for ticket sales
Marks the show-notes-to-ticket-page path ASPIRATIONAL rather than EXISTS
States that a path counts as EXISTS only when a mechanism carries a person or a file, not because a link exists
Points out that the cited agency case reports only channel-growth numbers with no ticket or registration figure attached to them
Does not present the 12,000 subscribers or the 40% view growth as evidence of ticket conversion
Writes the feed relationship in both directions, one line per path
Marks every path in the map EXISTS or ASPIRATIONAL
Includes event-to-channel paths covering finished recordings, the speaker pool to book from, and a reason to publish around an edition
Includes channel-to-event paths covering a warm first contact with a prospective speaker, cross-promotion inventory a swap can use, and a surface that keeps working in the gap
Argues reach and relationship value in place of a registration claim
Invents no conversion rate, attribution figure or funnel percentage
Does not decide here whether the channel is worth keeping in the portfolio, routing that to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-portfolio-strategy

evals.prompt: Maroua has hosted our show for four years and she is leaving in eleven weeks. The YouTube account and the podcast host are both under her personal Google account and her personal card. We have 61 episodes. Nobody else on the team has ever published an episode and we do not know who would take it over. What do we do in eleven weeks? I was going to add whoever volunteers as a second admin on her account and call it done.
evals.expected_output: A documented ownership and access transfer as the default, the second-admin plan named as the exact failure the transfer prevents, the closed-archive fold presented as a live option given no successor, no invented overlap window, and a dated handover document naming the release custodian.
expectations: Recommends the documented ownership and access transfer as the default rung
Names adding a second admin while the personal account stays owner of record as the failure the transfer exists to prevent
States that the property becomes unrecoverable the day that personal account closes
Requires moving every account off any individual's personal ownership, with a second named holder on each
Does not recommend the named-successor-with-overlap rung as the default, since no successor exists
Invents no overlap length, transfer window or notice period
Does not borrow a transfer window from samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-team-structure or samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-community-building
Presents folding into a closed archive as a live option, given 61 episodes and nobody named for the quiet months
States what a closing note must carry if the show folds: that it ended, the date, where the back-catalogue stays reachable, who holds the account, and where the audience should go instead
Names letting the feed lapse silently with no notice as a deleted option rather than a cheap version of the archive
Requires the guest-release records to get a named custodian with the retention decision restated rather than assumed inherited
Requires confirming that every published episode still resolves at its own address after the transfer, before the outgoing owner stops being reachable
Requires the handover document to be dated and to fix a date for re-checking it on a schedule
Requires recording what the show committed to publicly, so the incoming holder inherits the promise rather than discovering it

evals.prompt: We recorded 14 talks at our last edition and our editor has already cut audio-only versions of all 14. Somebody on the team said that is our podcast, just push them to Spotify. I want to do this properly: what mics should we buy for the interview episodes, what is the right DAW, and should we get a second recorder for redundancy? Also we need a name.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to specify equipment or editing tooling, the 14 cuts identified as one-edition derivatives rather than a channel, and the interview run before any posture is proposed, with archive-only as the likely default.
expectations: Declines to recommend specific microphones, recorders or editing software
Routes signal path, microphone count, redundancy and editing execution to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-production
States that the 14 audio cuts are samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-content-repurposing's artifact, not a channel
States that a derivative becomes an episode only once a property with its own format and cadence exists to receive it
Runs interview questions about the posture, the quiet-month owner and the gap between editions before producing a plan
Proposes the archive-only feed as the default posture, given derivatives already exist
States that an archive-only feed needs a durable address, a purpose line a stranger can read, and a named holder of the account
States that the archive-only feed makes no cadence promise
Does not substitute a naming or branding exercise for the posture decision
Promises no publishing rhythm for the interview episodes
Requires checking that the existing consent record covers publication before the 14 cuts are pushed anywhere

evals.prompt: Give me the one-liner we put on our site, plus our KPI sheet. The show is called Between Editions, run by our co-organizer Tomas, who has roughly three hours a week outside the two months around our conference. We want to commit publicly to something. For KPIs my co-founder wants subscriber growth targets, a listener-to-ticket conversion rate, and a rule that we drop the show if we miss three episodes in a row.
evals.expected_output: A cadence-commitment sentence carrying what publishes, the rhythm, its named owner and the missed-cycle behaviour; the three requested KPIs declined or reshaped; the three completeness gates and the self-set measures supplied instead.
expectations: Writes a cadence sentence carrying all four elements: what the show publishes, on what rhythm, who owns that rhythm, and what happens when a cycle is missed
Names Tomas as the owner inside the sentence
Does not produce an unowned rhythm promise of the 'new episodes every other week' shape
Derives any rhythm from the stated three hours a week and the two-month recovery window rather than from a generic publishing convention
Deliberately under-promises, on the grounds that the argued failure is a property that stops rather than one that publishes rarely
Declines the listener-to-ticket conversion rate as a measure, stating that no sourced figure ties channel activity to registrations
Declines to set a subscriber growth target
Declines the three-misses-in-a-row rule, stating that no numeric miss threshold is sourced
Treats a repeated miss as a demotion signal on the existence-posture menu rather than as a discipline problem
Reports pipeline depth as a count of guests named and agreed ahead of the next publish date, never as a rate
Includes the release-coverage gate: every published episode has an episode-specific release from every participant, on file with a named holder
Includes the named-quiet-month-owner gate, with the public cadence matching the one that person agreed to
Includes the handover-readiness gate: a dated handover document naming a living holder for the platform account, the feed and the release records
States the pass threshold as all three gates with zero exceptions

evals.prompt: Two asks landed this week. A newsletter called Platform Weekly wants to swap: they will plug our show if our lead organizer guests on their podcast. And the organizers of RustFest Iberia want to trade promotion, their audience for ours, and want me to negotiate the terms. Separately, our listeners keep emailing questions and I want to spin up a Discord so they can talk to each other and to guests, moderated by whoever is around. Tell me how to handle all three.
evals.expected_output: All three asks routed out: the barter to media partnerships, the swap negotiation to cross-event promotion, the Discord to community building, with what crosses each seam stated from this side only.
expectations: Does not broker or negotiate the Platform Weekly barter
Routes the Platform Weekly exchange to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-media-partnerships
Identifies the organizer guesting on Platform Weekly's podcast as an appearance on someone else's show, distinct from this property
Routes the RustFest Iberia swap negotiation to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@cross-event-promotion
States that this side supplies the episode or the date for such a swap and does not negotiate its terms
Routes the Discord to samber/dev-event-organizer-skills@event-community-building
States that publishing at people is not a space they belong to
Names the need for a member list, replies or moderation as the signal that the object has become the community's rather than the show's
Does not produce a moderation plan, membership retention duty or member-list design
Rejects 'whoever is around' as a moderation arrangement rather than accepting it
Keeps a new-episode notice as content that can cross into that space
Keeps guests or topics surfaced in that space as input this side still sources and vets

evals.prompt: We run four events a year: two meetups, a hackathon, and a two-day conference. My co-organizer Ines already hosts a weekly show of her own, and we have a part-time editor on retainer for 10 hours a month, paid out of the conference budget. Ines wants to go weekly with a conference-branded show and says it is obviously the best option because it reaches the most people. The rest of the team thinks she is wrong. Settle it.
evals.expected_output: Brainstorming mode rather than a verdict: candidate shapes with trade-offs, the heavy-cadence promotion conditions checked one by one, the reach argument rejected because reach tracks effort exactly, and the existing assets named as the answers that moved specific rungs.
expectations: Enters brainstorming mode with two or three candidate shapes and their trade-offs, rather than issuing a single verdict, because the team disagrees on whether to run the channel at all
Asks questions one at a time and validates each section before moving to the next
States the heavy-cadence rung's promotion conditions as a set that must all hold, not as a single test
Names the funded-or-committed owner condition, the in-house editor or co-organizer who already hosts a show condition, and the compounding condition
Identifies the retained editor and Ines's existing weekly show as satisfying the in-house asset condition, and says which answer moved which rung
Requires the one-off versus compounding answer before promoting the heavy rung
Rejects 'it reaches the most people' as sufficient grounds, on the basis that reach tracks effort exactly across the menu
States that efficiency never picks the heavy-cadence rung, because it tops reach, effort and compliance cost together
Reports zero strict-dominance relations across the menu's pairs, so no rung dominates another
States that the dominance result is vacuous by construction here and is never a pass, so the ratios must be challenged directly
Names what the heavy rung is one step from becoming: a media operation with its own staffing question that no skill in this collection covers
Distinguishes standing roles filled for a stated period, one each for booking, recording, editing and publishing, from per-episode improvisation
States that one person holding every role is the low-cadence rung with an unsustainable rhythm attached, not the heavy rung
Presents the outcome section by section, with approval sought per section
